title: Why Services? 🔌
description: Discover why you can't rely on Pod IPs and how Services solve the problem.

slides.title: The Pod IP Problem 🎯
slides.content:
# Pods come and go

Every Pod gets its own IP address, but that IP is **ephemeral**:
- When a Pod is deleted and recreated (by a Deployment), it gets a new IP.
- If a node fails, Pods move to other nodes with new IPs.
- Scaling up creates new Pods with fresh IPs.

If your frontend app hard‑codes a backend Pod’s IP, it will break the moment that Pod restarts.

We need a **stable, permanent address** that always points to the right set of Pods. That’s what a Service provides.

quizData.question: Why can't you rely on a Pod's IP for long‑term connectivity?

options.text: Pod IPs change when Pods restart or are replaced
Pod IPs are only reachable from outside the cluster
Pod IPs are shared among all containers

quizData.explanation: Pods are ephemeral; a new Pod gets a new IP, so direct IP usage is fragile.

slides.title: What Is a Service? 🎛️
slides.content:
# A stable endpoint for a set of Pods

A Service is a Kubernetes object that:
- Gets a **permanent, virtual IP** (ClusterIP) – it never changes.
- Provides **load balancing** across a dynamic set of Pods matching a label selector.
- Automatically tracks which Pods are healthy (readiness probe) and routes only to ready ones.
- Offers different types of exposure: internal, node‑level, or cloud‑load‑balancer.

Think of it as a built‑in proxy that sits in front of your Pods.

slides.title: How Services Select Pods 🏷️
slides.content:
## Labels again!

A Service uses a `selector` (label query) to find the Pods that should receive traffic. Example:
```yaml
selector:
  app: backend
```
The Service will send traffic to any Pod in the same namespace that has the label `app: backend` and is **Ready**.

When Pods are added or removed (scale up/down), the Service automatically updates its list of endpoints.

quizData.question: What determines which Pods a Service routes traffic to?
quizData.explanation: The Service matches Pods by their labels, as defined in the selector field.

slides.title: Service Types Overview 🗺️
slides.content:
## Four main types

| Type          | Scope                     | Use Case                            |
|---------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **ClusterIP** | Internal only             | Backend‑to‑backend communication    |
| **NodePort**  | Node IP + static port     | Debugging, on‑premise access         |
| **LoadBalancer** | External IP via cloud LB  | Public internet traffic             |
| **ExternalName** | CNAME record            | Redirect to an external DNS name    |

We'll explore the first three in depth.

quizData.question: What does `kubectl expose` do?

options.text: Creates a Service that routes to the specified resource
Exposes a container port to the node

quizData.explanation: `expose` generates a Service based on a Deployment or Pod.
